UnitStatement: The appendix consolidates three layers of formally stated invariants governing the Chirality agent instruction architecture.
The invariant layers are organized by layer of origin and scope of application.
Workflow design requirements R1-R9 apply universally to all agents and workflow designs.
Decomposition invariants I1-I10 govern all decomposition agents.
System-wide invariants K-* are enforced across the full agent suite.
All cataloged invariants are reproduced faithfully from their authoritative source documents.
Workflow design requirements R1-R9 are defined in AGENT_HELPS_HUMANS.md.
A workflow design is compliant when all nine workflow design requirements are satisfied.
R1 requires human-owned decisions to be enumerated and preserved.
R2 requires task agents to run without mid-run human decisions.
R3 requires every agent to have an explicit write scope.
R3 requires tool roots to be isolated from source truth.
R4 requires each run to produce a new snapshot folder.
R4 permits pointer files to be overwritten while snapshots may not be overwritten.
R5 requires aggregated or extracted data to include SourcePath and best-effort SectionRef.
R6 requires missing data to become TBD with assumptions captured.
R7 prevents the system from hiding or silently resolving discrepancies unless explicitly directed.
R8 requires pipelines to have a defined brief format and deterministic outputs.
R9 requires version-control publishing to be reviewable and non-destructive by default.
Decomposition invariants I1-I10 are defined in AGENT_DECOMP_BASE.md.
Decomposition invariants apply to PROJECT_DECOMP, SOFTWARE_DECOMP, and DOMAIN_DECOMP.
AUDIT_DECOMP verifies decomposition invariants.
I1-I10 must hold across conforming decomposition agents regardless of domain.
I1 requires the structured outline and decomposition to be confirmed by the human at defined gates.
I1 prohibits skipping decomposition gates.
I2 prohibits creating atomic units, objectives, partitions, production units, or artifacts beyond source material and user intent support.
I2 requires unknown decomposition content to be marked TBD and surfaced as an open issue.
I3 prohibits nested partitions.
I3 requires additional granularity to be proposed as same-level partitions.
I4 requires every IN-scope atomic unit to be assigned to exactly one partition.
I4 requires ambiguous partition assignments to be forced decisions resolved by the human at gates.
I5 requires assigned IDs to remain stable across revisions unless the human explicitly requests renumbering.
I6 requires each production unit ID to be mechanically derived from its parent partition ID.
I6 treats the domain-specific coupling format as variable while preserving ID coupling as invariant.
I7 requires objectives to be derived from source material.
I7 requires unmapped objectives to be surfaced as open issues.
I8 requires non-trivial assignment decisions to be recorded as explicit decisions in decomposition output.
I9 requires every decomposition to include a machine-checkable ledger.
I9 requires every decomposition to include a Coverage & Telemetry summary.
I9 uses the ledger and telemetry summary to make coverage provable and quality comparable across revisions.
I10 requires every decomposition to include a Vocabulary Map.
I10 requires canonical terms to be used consistently.
I10 requires synonyms to be mapped.
I10 requires semantic drift to be prevented.
System-wide invariants K-* are defined in CONTRACT.md.
System-wide invariant IDs are stable and never reused.
Retired system-wide invariants are relocated to the retired section of CONTRACT.md with retirement rationale.
K-HIER-1 requires projects to be decomposed as packages containing deliverables.
K-HIER-1 requires project decomposition to be flat, with no nesting and no phases layer.
K-ID-1 requires deliverable IDs to be stable and persist across path changes.
K-ID-1 treats path as a physical projection of decomposition rather than identity.
K-AUTH-1 reserves binding approval record authorship to humans.
K-AUTH-1 prohibits agents from claiming to certify, approve, sign, seal, or issue work for reliance.
K-AUTH-2 requires approvals to bind to a specific git SHA.
K-AUTH-2 makes content change after approval void the approval.
K-BIND-1 requires approvals to be always binding and only binding.
K-BIND-1 allows non-binding guidance outside approval records.
K-SEAL-1 prohibits Type 2 agent execution before context is sealed and gate-approved by a human.
K-GHOST-1 limits Type 2 agent context to folder contents plus declared references.
K-GHOST-1 prohibits ghost inputs.
K-DEP-1 makes deliverable-local _DEPENDENCIES.md and Dependencies.csv authoritative for dependencies.
K-DEP-1 rejects a central dependency graph.
K-DEP-1 makes dependency aggregation on-demand through _Reconciliation/.
K-DEP-2 requires dependency references to deliverables to resolve to existing deliverable IDs.
K-DEP-2 requires unresolvable dependency targets to use TargetType=UNKNOWN.
K-STATUS-1 makes _STATUS.md the canonical human-readable lifecycle state file for each deliverable.
K-STATUS-1 says no other file determines deliverable state.
K-STALE-1 propagates upstream-change staleness to all transitive dependent deliverables.
K-STALE-2 requires stale items to be triaged by a human before being considered current.
K-STALE-2 defines stale-item resolution modes as no impact, needs rework, or needs review.
K-VAL-1 marks a deliverable dirty when any governed input changed since its last approved SHA.
K-GATE-1 makes gates dynamic per project instance.
K-GATE-1 sets the minimum required gates as seal transition and pipeline run approval.
K-GATE-1 allows additional gates to be project-configurable.
K-MERGE-1 allows merge to main only when branch HEAD equals the approved SHA for the relevant run.
K-PROV-1 requires every extracted dependency row to cite evidence.
K-PROV-1 accepts EvidenceFile plus SourceRef, or explicit location TBD, as dependency evidence.
K-INVENT-1 requires unknown values to become TBD rather than guessed.
K-INVENT-1 prohibits agents from inventing scope items, dependency targets, parameter values, or engineering content.
K-CONFLICT-1 requires conflicts between sources to be surfaced rather than silently resolved.
K-CONFLICT-1 requires agents to expose disagreements with pointers to the conflicting sources.
K-CLAIM-1 prohibits claims, conclusions, and characterizations from overstating available warrant.
K-CLAIM-1 allows necessity, sufficiency, universality, completeness, exclusivity, or direct regulatory conclusiveness only when cited evidence supports that strength.
K-CLAIM-1 otherwise frames claims as interpretation, implementation-specific design, or proposal.
K-WRITE-1 requires every agent to declare an explicit write scope in its header block.
K-WRITE-1 prohibits agents from writing outside their declared zones.
K-SNAP-1 makes task-agent outputs to tool roots immutable snapshots.
K-SNAP-1 permits pointer files such as _LATEST.md to be overwritten.
K-SNAP-1 prohibits snapshot folders from being overwritten.
The Enforcement Map Summary is reproduced from CONTRACT.md Section 2.
The Enforcement Map Summary maps each enforcement point to the invariants it checks.
Agent instructions are a design-time enforcement point that constrains intent rather than guaranteed behavior.
Agent instructions check K-GHOST-1, K-WRITE-1, K-SNAP-1, K-PROV-1, K-INVENT-1, K-CONFLICT-1, K-CLAIM-1, K-DEP-1, and K-DEP-2.
ORCHESTRATOR is a runtime enforcement point for K-SEAL-1, K-GATE-1, and K-HIER-1.
Human review is a gate enforcement point for K-AUTH-1, K-AUTH-2, K-BIND-1, K-STALE-2, K-MERGE-1, K-VAL-1, and K-STATUS-1.
Future tooling is an automated enforcement point for K-STALE-1, K-VAL-1, K-MERGE-1, K-AUTH-2, and K-DEP-2.
PROJECT_DECOMP is a decomposition enforcement point for K-HIER-1 and K-ID-1.
